        位于莫干山路126号的阜丰（ Fou Foong ）面粉厂约850名工人，以及位于澳门路12/12号的信大（ Sing Dah ）面粉厂180名工人，于1939年9月7日午夜12时宣布“怠工”罢工，以强制实施以下要求：

    1. 每位工人每月发放津贴5元。

    2. 外籍磨粉师不得殴打和辱骂工人。

    3. 管理层不得无故解雇工人。

    4. 重新开放工人子弟学校。

        阜丰面粉厂的工人于今晨（9月8日）向工业科提交请愿书，请求调解。

        本人于今日下午前往工厂拜访了管理层代表孙伯屏（ Y. P. Sun ）先生。孙先生表示，工人在宣布罢工前未向管理层提出任何要求，此举违反了中华民国国民政府颁布的《工厂法》，因此管理层决定解雇19名罢工领袖，并请求警务处依据《工厂法》第73条和第74条在法庭上对罢工领袖采取行动。然而，他继续说道，管理层希望工业科能调解此纠纷，如果工人立即复工，管理层将考虑工人的要求。

        本人拜访了工人代表，试图说服他们复工，同时在达成解决方案之前与管理层进行谈判。工人坚持要求先释放被警方逮捕的八名代表，然后才肯复工并与管理层谈判。已要求工人派出三名代表，并联系工业科商讨复工事宜。

Trouble at Foh Sing Flour Mill.

At 6-10 a.m. on 23/8/39 a telephone message
was received at this station from a foreman named
Yue Kyung Yu (虞敬之), employed in the Foh Sing (福新)
No. 7 Flour Mill, No. 80, Lane 1073, Chengtu Road,
to the effect that workers at above address were
being instigated to go on strike. S.I. Alexandroff,
S.I. Wong, and C.D.C. 38 proceeded to the scene,
where on arrival it was found that work was proceeding
as usual, no signs of trouble being observed.

From enquiries made by C.D.C. 38 and the under-
signed, it was ascertained that about 160 transport-
ation coolies employed in above flour mill were
granted a wage increase of 17.5% on 10/7/39, but
on 17/8/39 declared a strike in order to enforce
a demand for an additional increase of 2.5%, which
was granted. (See Daily Intelligence Reports of
13/7/39, 19/8/39, and 23/8/39.) About 6 a.m. on
23/8/39 one of these coolies named Ma Siau Foo (馬小富),
30, Kompo, incited the remainder to demand that the
management supply each man with a sack of flour free
of charge. The foreman, Yue Kyung Yu, then telephoned
the station, but before the arrival of police, Ma
Siau Foo left the scene, while the other

Some of the transportation coolies employed by
Fon Sin Flour Mill No.7, Lane 1073/5 Mengtsu Road, declared
a strike this morning, August 17, in order to enforce a demand
for an additional increase of 2.5% in wages, since they heard
that the management have granted 20% increase of wages to the
employees and other mill coolies on August 15, 1939. The
Industrial Section was asked for mediation. After negotia-

work in the afternoon on my advice pending a settlement.

UNREST AMONG FLOUR MILL
Transportation Coolies

The representatives of flour mill transportation
coolies had a meeting with the representative of flour mill
management, Mr. Wang (王堯臣) at Foh Sing Flour Mill No.7,
Lane 1073, 50 Chengtu Road, on July 8, 1939, negotiating
on increase of wage rates for transportation of wheat and
flour per bag from the creek to mill godown. The manage-
ment agreed to increase wage rates by ten percent but the
representatives of transportation coolies were not satisfied
with the amount of increase, and another meeting was arranged
between two parties at 12 o'clock this noon at the same
place for further negotiation.

The representatives of flour mill transportation
coolies sent a request for mediation to the Industrial
Section, if they fail to reach any conclusion at to-day's
meeting.

July 11, 1939.

The representatives of transportation coolies and
of flour mill managements met yesterday noon at Foh Sing
Flour Mill No.7, Lane 1073, 50 Chengtu Road. An increase
of 17.5% on wage rates for transportation of wheat and flour
bags from the creek to mills and godowns has been agreed by
both parties, and a written agreement will be signed by the
representatives of both parties at this noon, at the same
place.

G. Y. Koo

INDUSTRIAL UNREST AMONG FLOUR MILL
TRANSPORTATION COOLIES

I called on the management of the following flour
mills to-day:

Foh Sing (福新二廠) Flour Mill No.2, 5 West
Soochow Road

Foh Sing (福新七廠) Flour Mill No.7, Lane 1073/50
Chengtu Road

Fou Foong (阜丰) Flour Mill, 126 Mokanshan Road.

Sing Dah (信大) Flour Mill, 10 Macao Road

Hwa Foong (華丰) Flour Mill, 289 Ferry Road.

Some 800 male transportation coolies employed by
the above mentioned flour mills have submitted to their
respective managements, on June 29, 1939, a written request
for a 40% increase in wages owing to the present high cost
of living. Although the coolies are directly employed by
the mills, they are under the control of foreman or "Kung
Tou" (工头) of each mill. Their wages are paid on the
wage rates fixed by the mill management and "Kung Tou"
before the hostilities.

The representatives of the above mills said that
the requests are now under consideration by the mill
authorities, who will call a meeting discussing the matter
this week. They were asked to send in a copy of wage rates
of transporting wheat and flour per bag.

July 5, 1939.

Wong (王全旺), at Lane 1034, 23 Tonquin Road, to-day. He
said that he will inform the representatives of the other
mills to call in this office to-morrow morning at 9:30.

At 4.50 pem. the same day, the Industrial and Social 
Division representative called on Mr. Russel Y. Sun,manager, at

At 8.00 a.m. December 16th, the 1,000 male workers 
of the mill gathered in the compound of the mill, md a sit down 
strike was declared.

The Division has made 2: study of tha actual earnings 
and real wage indices of the workers of both the Fou Foong 
and Sing Dah Flour Mills as compared with those of the Foh 
Sing Nos. 2 and 8 Flour Mills for the month of August, 1940. 
It appeares that the former mills have done very well. The 
real wage indices of the various types of work range from 70 
to 80, whereas the general real wage index for the city was 
about 44 in November. These first two mills were much better 
"payers" than the Foh Sing Mills. 


At 35.50 pom. the same day, the irdustrial and Social 
Division representative proceeded to the mill and informed 
some 800 workers gathered inside the mill sompound that their 
demands had been rejected by the management. Efforts were 
made to persuade the workers to resume work in order to avoid 
a deadlock, but with no result. Until 6.00 pem. some 200 
workers gathered outside the looked mill gates, where uniformed 
police and detectives were posted, and wished to enter the 
mill compound to join the others. They requested the Division 
representative to negotiate with the police to permit them 
to go inside. They would make a rush if they were refused. 
In order to avoid conflict between the strikers and the police 
outside the locked gates, efforts were made to persuade those 
gathered outside to remain in their place, and with the 
permission of the police, a workers' representative was allowed 
to pass through the gates to make communication between the 
two groups of strikers. Thus they were satisfied and remained 
quietly in the mill compound. At 7.00 pom. the Industrial 
Division represnetative left the mill premises.

tion of rice, and leave the other demands for the further 


consideration of the management. It was pointed out to the 
workers that they had been accorded reasonable treatment and 
that while the mill was short of wheat, they should realise 
the actual situation and not make further demands. The 

mana zement were informed of the worker's attitude, but refused 
to consider any demands and deoided to dismiss 31 workers

On December 19th, a notice was posted at the entrance 
to the mill stating that those workers willing to return to 
work under the management's conditions with regard to the 
supply of rice and flour, might apply for registration. Some 
248 workers registered that day. 


On December 24th, registration continued and reached 
a total of some 700 workers. 


Up to December 28th, all the workers of the mill 
had registered with the management with the exception of some 
31 agitators, whom the management intended to dismiss.

The dispute, therefore, is concluded.
